definitions.explanation: A wide version of the traditional wooden veranda ({縁側|えんがわ}), broad enough to set out a table and chairs. Common in ryokan and Japanese-style guest rooms.

examples.japanese: {広縁|ひろえん}でお{茶|ちゃ}を{飲|の}む。
examples.english: To drink tea on the wide veranda.

examples.japanese: この{部屋|へや}には{広縁|ひろえん}が{付|つ}いている。
examples.english: This room has a wide veranda.

examples.japanese: {旅館|りょかん}の{広縁|ひろえん}から{庭園|ていえん}を{眺|なが}めるのは{格別|かくべつ}だ。
examples.english: Gazing at the garden from the ryokan's wide veranda is something special.

notes:
A wide {縁側|えんがわ} — the wooden veranda strip along a Japanese-style room — broad enough to hold a small table and chairs. Frequently found in ryokan guest rooms as a relaxing spot beside the window.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {広縁|ひろえん}{付|つ}きの{部屋|へや}: a room with a wide veranda
- {広縁|ひろえん}でくつろぐ: to relax on the wide veranda

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {縁側|えんがわ}: engawa — the standard, narrower wooden veranda
- ベランダ: balcony — a modern outdoor platform, not the wooden interior-edge veranda
